## portcheck list

List sockets and the processes that own them

### Synopsis

List local TCP and UDP sockets together with their owning process.

Without elevated privileges some owners may be hidden; portcheck prints a hint
when that happens.

```
portcheck list [flags]
```

### Examples

```
  portcheck list --listening
  portcheck list --port 3000-3999 --proto tcp
  portcheck list --name 'node*' --json
  portcheck list -l --watch 2s
  portcheck list -l --wide        # who started each process, and its command line
```

### Options

```
  -h, --help             help for list
  -l, --listening        only sockets accepting connections (TCP LISTEN, unconnected UDP)
      --name string      only processes whose name matches this glob (case-insensitive)
      --pid int32Slice   only sockets owned by these PIDs (default [])
      --port string      local ports, e.g. 80,443,8000-8100 or a preset (common, well-known, ...)
      --proto strings    protocols to include: tcp, udp
      --state strings    only these states, e.g. LISTEN,ESTABLISHED
      --watch duration   refresh every interval until interrupted, e.g. 2s
  -w, --wide             also show the parent process and command line
```

### Options inherited from parent commands

```
      --json                shorthand for --output json
      --log-format string   log format: text or json (default "text")
      --no-color            disable colors (also honors NO_COLOR)
  -o, --output string       output format: table, plain, csv, json (default: table on a terminal, plain otherwise)
  -v, --verbose             log diagnostic details to stderr
```
